item.title: Filter
item.description:
Development reference · Larecs 1.0.0b1 · revision 8d289cca4516. Host threading and device execution are experimental. Compatibility and status.

Mojo structSource

Filter

@memory_only
struct Filter[_include: Components[_include.ComponentTypes] = Components(), _exclude: Components[_exclude.ComponentTypes] = Components(), _is_exclusive: Bool = False, _read: Components[_read.ComponentTypes] = Components(), _written: Components[_written.ComponentTypes] = Components()]

Compile-time component inclusion and exclusion spec used to build queries.

Every included component is tracked separately as readable (_read) and/or writable (_written). include – the default, and the only mode that matters for the host query API, where this distinction is not used – marks a component both readable and writable, matching this type’s behavior before _read/_written existed. read and write mark a component for one direction only: a kernel running on the device then only pays for the transfer direction it actually needs (see SystemContext.run), and EntityAccessor.get/set enforce the declared mode at compile time, not just by convention – see read and write below.

Build a filter by chaining include, read, write, exclude, and exclusive, then call the result, as in Filter().include[Position].read[Velocity](). Each step names a new Filter type; the trailing () constructs the filter value that queries and kernels take. Without it, the compiler reports failed to infer parameter '_include'. Calling every step, as in Filter().include[Position]().exclude[Velocity](), builds the same filter.

A named filter can be extended, which lets several systems share a base filter:

@fieldwise_init
struct Position(Copyable, Movable):
    var x: Float64
    var y: Float64

@fieldwise_init
struct Velocity(Copyable, Movable):
    var dx: Float64
    var dy: Float64

@fieldwise_init
struct Frozen(Copyable, Movable):
    pass

comptime moving = Filter().include[Position].read[Velocity]()
comptime moving_unfrozen = moving.exclude[Frozen]()

def main() raises:
    var world = World[Position, Velocity, Frozen]()
    _ = world.storage.add_entity(Position(0, 0), Velocity(1, 0))
    _ = world.storage.add_entity(Position(0, 0), Velocity(1, 0), Frozen())
    assert_equal(len(world.storage.query[moving]()), 2)
    assert_equal(len(world.storage.query[moving_unfrozen]()), 1)

Aliases

include

Returns a Filter also including the given component types for both reading and writing.

include[*ComponentTypes: ComponentType]: AnyStruct[Filter[Components(), _exclude, _is_exclusive, Components(), Components()]] = Filter[Components(), _exclude, _is_exclusive, Components(), Components()]

read

Returns a Filter also including the given component types, accessible only for reading.

read[*ComponentTypes: ComponentType]: AnyStruct[Filter[Components(), _exclude, _is_exclusive, Components(), _written]] = Filter[Components(), _exclude, _is_exclusive, Components(), _written]

EntityAccessor.get returns an immutable reference for these components; EntityAccessor.set is a compile error. SystemContext.run’s device path uploads these components before the kernel runs but does not download them afterward, since a read-only kernel cannot have changed them.

write

Returns a Filter also including the given component types, accessible only for writing.

write[*ComponentTypes: ComponentType]: AnyStruct[Filter[Components(), _exclude, _is_exclusive, _read, Components()]] = Filter[Components(), _exclude, _is_exclusive, _read, Components()]

EntityAccessor.set overwrites these components; EntityAccessor.get is a compile error, since a write-only component’s prior value is never uploaded to the kernel. SystemContext.run’s device path downloads these components after the kernel runs but does not upload them beforehand, since a write-only kernel never reads their prior value.

exclude

Returns a Filter also excluding the given component types.

exclude[*ComponentTypes: ComponentType]: AnyStruct[Filter[_include, Components(), _is_exclusive, _read, _written]] = Filter[_include, Components(), _is_exclusive, _read, _written]

exclusive

Returns a Filter that matches only entities with exactly the included components.

exclusive = Filter[_include, _is_exclusive=True, _read=_read, _written=_written]

exclusive discards the component types excluded so far, because an exclusive filter already rejects every component it does not include. Filter().include[B]().exclude[A]().exclusive() therefore holds no excluded types, while Filter().include[B]().exclusive().exclude[A]() holds A; both match only entities whose components are exactly B.

reads

Returns whether this filter allows reading component T.

reads[T: ComponentType]: Bool = TypeList.contains[T]()

Returns: True when T is accessible for reading, via read or include.

writes

Returns whether this filter allows writing component T.

writes[T: ComponentType]: Bool = TypeList.contains[T]()

Returns: True when T is accessible for writing, via write or include.

Parameters

  • _include (Components[_include.ComponentTypes]): The component types that must be present.
  • _exclude (Components[_exclude.ComponentTypes]): The component types that must be absent.
  • _is_exclusive (Bool): Whether only the included components may be present.
  • _read (Components[_read.ComponentTypes]): The included component types accessible for reading.
  • _written (Components[_written.ComponentTypes]): The included component types accessible for writing.
